behavior.arguments: rdi = destination base; rsi = source base. Four qwords are read at [rsi+0x00..0x18] and four qwords are written at [rdi+0x00..0x18]. No other argument is read and no other field is written.

edges.order_reversal_only: with source qwords [1, 2, 3, 4] the destination becomes [0x0400000000000000, 0x0300000000000000, 0x0200000000000000, 0x0100000000000000]: reversal and swap compose, neither alone explains the output.
edges.single_byte: with source [0x00000000000000ff, 0, 0, 0] the destination is [0, 0, 0, 0xff00000000000000]: the low byte of the first source qword becomes the high byte of the last destination qword.
edges.zero: with all source qwords 0 the destination is all 0.

behavior.entry_shape: Opens with mov 0x18(%rsi),%rax (NOT endbr64); zero branches, zero calls inside; a single ret.
behavior.return_rule: [rdi+0x00] = bswap([rsi+0x18]), [rdi+0x08] = bswap([rsi+0x10]), [rdi+0x10] = bswap([rsi+0x08]), [rdi+0x18] = bswap([rsi+0x00]); each bswap reverses the byte order of one 64-bit word. The copy is 32 bytes total with reversed order and reversed byte order.

coordinate_system: ELF virtual addresses, without a guessed loader or Ghidra rebase. The ELF section table maps .text with file offset = VA - 0x1000; the retained .eh_frame has equal file offset and VA. The tools resolve sections rather than assuming one global VA/file-offset relationship.

incoming_pattern_scan.note: Byte-pattern scan over the full .text section (70,370,352 bytes) for e8 sites whose rel32 lands on the window start; exactly two sites found, each boundary-confirmed inside its own caller FDE. This is explicitly not a complete xref census: indirect calls, tail jumps, and PLT references are out of scope for the scan.
incoming_pattern_scan.relocation_note: No R_X86_64_RELATIVE record in any .rela.* section names this window as addend (full-section scan: 80,022 .rela.dyn + 278 .rela.plt entries).
